Jinny Lu placed second in 2025. (Kent Porter / The Press Democrat) By Charles Swanson | charles.swanson@pressdemocrat.com | The Press Democrat PUBLISHED: August 21, 2026 at 12:56 PM PDT | UPDATED: August 21, 2026 at 1:14 PM PDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Jinny Lu, a 6-year-old pug from Ukiah by way of Los Angeles and South Korea, took her unconventional beauty to a national stage this week following her victory at the 2026 World’s Ugliest Dog Contest . After being crowned the champion Friday, Aug.14, at the Sonoma County Fair in Santa Rosa, the celebrated rescue dog and her owner, Michelle Grady, traveled to New York City for a featured appearance Monday morning, Aug. 17, on NBC’s “Today” show. “It was a complete whirlwind, but joyful,” said Grady, who runs the Pug Hotel senior dog sanctuary in Ukiah . “In what lifetime did I ever expect this to happen?” During the broadcast, “Today” anchors Craig Melvin, Sheinelle Jones and Carson Daly, along with correspondents Dylan Dreyer, Savannah Sellers and Gadi Schwartz, fawned over Jinny Lu’s adorable hanging tongue and penchant for drooling. Schwartz, who was one of the judges at Friday’s contest, had traveled to Santa Rosa with his family to cover the competition. Grady also unveiled Jinny Lu’s latest necklace, commemorating her win after three previous appearances in the contest. Ukiah pug Jinny Lu, 2026 World’s Ugliest Dog Contest winner, and her owner Michelle Grady of The Pug Hotel senior dog sanctuary, join the cast of the “Today” show during a broadcast at NBC’s studio in Manhattan, Monday, Aug. 17, 2026. (Michelle Grady) "Today" show correspondent Gadi Schwartz — who traveled to Santa Rosa with his family to cover the 2026 World’s Ugliest Dog Contest — holds winner Jinny Lu backstage at NBC's studios in Manhattan before the Ukiah pug and owner Michelle Grady appeared on the show, Monday morning, Aug. 17, 2026. (Michelle Grady) Ukiah pug Jinny Lu, the 2026 World’s Ugliest Dog Contest winner, checks herself in the mirror backstage before her featured appearance on NBC’s “Today” show, Monday Aug. 17, 2026, in New York City. (Michelle Grady) Grady said she never expected her beloved pug to win, but attributes Jinny Lu’s victory to her personality. “She’s got her silly tongue, but I feel like it’s more the way she looks into people’s eyes,” Grady said. “She genuinely wants to be held by people, and different people.” Jinny Lu appeared to enjoy her newfound fame. She loved the crowds at Friday’s competition and embraced the attention in New York, where she and Grady saw “The Outsiders” on Broadway, walked around Times Square and met fans who recognized her on the street and asked to hold her for photographs. Ukiah pug Jinny Lu, the 2026 World’s Ugliest Dog Contest winner, explores Manhattan, Sunday, Aug. 16, during a trip to New York City for a featured appearance on NBC’s “Today” show on Monday morning. (Michelle Grady) “Every five steps, we were stopped because somebody wanted their picture taken with Jinny Lu, and that’s before the ‘Today’ show (broadcast),” Grady said. “I couldn’t have been more stunned that Jinny was famous.” The attention is a long way from Jinny Lu’s beginnings. Four years ago, volunteers with Pug Rescue of Korea rescued her from a small wooden box in South Korea. Grady later adopted her through the Los Angeles-based rescue organization. “I took one look at her and said, ‘That’s my pug,’” Grady said. “And I’m forever grateful because she’s such an important part of our grumble.” Jinny Lu, the 2026 World’s Ugliest Dog Contest winner, at the Pug Hotel senior dog sanctuary in Ukiah. (Michelle Grady) Jinny Lu, center, cuddles with fellow pugs at the Pug Hotel senior dog sanctuary in Ukiah. (Michelle Grady) As the contest winner, Jinny Lu received $5,000 in prize money, which is being donated to the Pug Hotel to help the nonprofit provide sanctuary for senior pugs and to rehabilitate, foster and rehome pugs in need, Grady said. Jinny Lu will also appear on limited-edition cans of MUG Root Beer, which sponsored the contest. When she’s not competing, Jinny Lu serves as an ambassador for the Pug Hotel, which Grady relocated from Rohnert Park to Ukiah in April. She frequently visits elementary schools with Grady to teach children about pet rescue and visits hospice patients and people in memory care facilities. “These pugs are so healing,” Grady said. “When you hold Jinny Lu, it just sort of lowers your heart rate.” The World’s Ugliest Dog Contest, a nearly 50-year tradition produced by the Sonoma-Marin Agricultural Association, celebrates dogs’ individual quirks and imperfections while promoting rescue and adoption. At this year’s competition, Jinny Lu beat eight other contestants, including dogs from as far away as Poland, to take the title. “This event has always been about celebrating the dogs that might otherwise be overlooked,” Mandy Clendenen, CEO of the Sonoma-Marin Agricultural Association, said in an Aug. 15 news release. For Jinny Lu, though, the national spotlight appears to be just another opportunity to do what she has always done best: make people want to pick her up. And, apparently, take her picture. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o.text: The Labour MP Clive Lewis, who was among the delegation, said: ‘We were detained, taken aside, and then interrogated.’ Photograph: Jonathan Brady/PA View image in fullscreen The Labour MP Clive Lewis, who was among the delegation, said: ‘We were detained, taken aside, and then interrogated.’ Photograph: Jonathan Brady/PA West Bank British politicians among international delegates barred from entering West Bank Group was on visit to meet Palestinian children, farmers and civil leaders facing escalating violence from Israeli forces Sinéad Campbell Mon 26 Oct 2026 17.39 EDT Last modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 18.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An international delegation including British politicians has been barred from entering the West Bank on a trip to meet Palestinian children, farmers and society leaders facing escalating violence from Israeli forces during olive harvest season. The delegation of 23 people, including four elected representatives, was drawn from countries including France, Spain, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Greece, Holland, Ireland and the US. It included the Labour MP Clive Lewis, the Scottish National party MP Lara Bird, the Scottish Greens MSP Kate Nevens and the former Labour MP Sam Tarry. Lewis told the Guardian: “We were detained, taken aside and then interrogated. I use the word interrogated because people were shouted at. We were asked why we were going in, what was happening, why our stories were one way or the other. The bottom line was it was a deeply unpleasant experience.” The delegates were set to participate in Progressive International’s Second Ramallah Congress, a gathering to oppose Israeli occupation in Palestine . The congress was organised by Progressive International in partnership with Birzeit University and includes a programme of meetings with Palestinian academics, students and civil society organisations. Tarry told the Guardian that he thought the delegation had a “genuine chance of going across” into the West Bank but they were detained at the Allenby/King Hussein Bridge by Israeli forces in Jordan for nine hours. “They made a political decision very clearly based on the fact they didn’t want people to witness what’s been going on in the West Bank, especially ahead of the elections,” he added. The exclusions occurred amid attacks by Israeli forces on Palestinian olive farmers and foreign press and activists in the region. International travel to parts of the West Bank is permitted but subject to military checkpoints. Earlier this month, Israeli media reported that the defence minister, Israel Katz, had instructed officials to pursue exclusion orders against activists travelling to Palestinian olive-harvesting areas. Guardian reporter filmed masked militants seconds before West Bank attack on French mayor Read more In the first two weeks of October, the UN aid coordination office recorded at least 160 Israeli settler attacks linked to the olive harvest, often under the protection or with the participation of Israeli forces. Israeli forces attacked European diplomats and a French mayor accompanying Palestinian farmers, while about 80 olive-harvest volunteers, including US congressional candidate Brad Lander, were also recently detained . Bird said in a statement: “I came to stand alongside Palestinians being attacked for harvesting olives on their own land. Instead, we were turned away at the border with no reason given. “It is more important now than ever that we bear witness and show our solidarity. But we were prevented from doing so. If Israel has nothing to hide, why is it so determined to stop us seeing what is happening in the occupied West Bank?” Laila Hazaineh, a political coordinator for Progressive International, said in a statement: “Despite escalating violence, our delegation remained determined to cross to Palestine to participate in the olive harvest, and actively engage with Palestinian communities and institutions. Every refusal of entry will only strengthen this determination.” The embassy of Israel has been contacted for comment. Argentina: Pope Leo XIV welcomed by Javier Milei for historic visit Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 9 November 2026 - 8:52 GMT+1 Pope Leo XIV has arrived in Argentina, on Sunday 8 November, for the first papal visit to the country in nearly 40 years. President Javier Milei welcomed him at Buenos Aires airport, while the city's iconic obelisk was illuminated in his honour. … More Argentine President Javier Milei welcomed Pope Leo XIV at Jorge Newbery Airport, where the two leaders shook hands before standing side by side on a red carpet for an official ceremony featuring the national guard. The pope also greeted Karina Milei , the president's sister and secretary general of the presidency, Argentina's senior clergy and a group of children and young people on the tarmac. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT That night the Obelisco was illuminated with a projection of the pontiff's face , the first switch-on in a city-wide illumination of monuments and façades, from the Floralis Genérica and Planetario to the Teatro Colón and Cabildo , dressed in Vatican yellow and white. The four-day visit , the first papal trip to Argentina since John Paul II in 1987 , is the second leg of a 12-day tour that began in Uruguay and ends in Peru . It resonates because Argentina is the homeland of his predecessor, Pope Francis, who never returned during his 12-year papacy. The meeting with Milei, whose austerity has reshaped the economy, produced a pointed contrast: the pope said "the economy must serve the person, not the person." https://www.thetablet.co.uk/news/polish-.text: Polish bishop convicted for failing to report abuse in unprecedented trial Adam Easton 29 October 2026, The Tablet Prev Next Bishop Andrzej Jeż, 63, has served as led the Diocese of Tarnów since 2012. Jarosław Kruk / Wikimedia Commons In 2017, Poland introduced criminal liability and a maximum sentence of three years in prison for anyone who fails to report a crime immediately despite having reliable information about that crime. A Polish court convicted a bishop of failing to notify law enforcement agencies about the alleged sexual abuse of children by two priests, in the first case of its kind. On Thursday, the District Court in Tarnów in southern Poland sentenced Bishop Andrzej Jeż of Tarnów to two years’ restriction of liberty by means of a 25 per cent deduction from his salary, to be sent to the Empowering Children Foundation. He denied both charges and the Tarnów Diocese Curia said it would appeal against the verdict. Prosecutors had asked the court for a sentence of 10 months in prison suspended for three years. In 2017, Poland introduced criminal liability and a maximum sentence of three years in prison for anyone who fails to immediately report a crime despite having reliable information about that crime. Before 2017, reporting a crime was considered a social duty, not a legal obligation. The case concerned two priests, identified under Polish law as Stanisław P. and Fr. Tomasz K., who were accused of sexually abusing dozens of children under the age of 15. Bishop Jeż only notified law enforcement agencies of the alleged crimes more than three years after the law took effect. Proceedings against Stanisław P. were discontinued in 2022 due to the statute of limitations, as the alleged crimes took place before 2017. He has since been laicised. The proceedings against Fr. Tomasz K. are pending. Bishop Jeż, 63, has served as led the Diocese of Tarnów since 2012. He is the first bishop to be tried in Poland for failing to report information about priests sexually abusing children . “The judgment is not final and does not definitively determine the criminal liability of Bishop Andrzej Jeż. The defence lawyers will request a written justification of the judgment, and after reviewing its content and detailed analysis, an appeal will be made,” the Tarnów Curia said in a statement. It said some of Stanisław P.’s alleged crimes took place when he was serving as a priest in Ukraine and they were reported to the relevant Ukrainian authorities. It said Bishop Jeż first learnt of the allegations in 2019. The diocese initiated internal Church procedures and after verifying the information, Bishop Jeż’s delegate informed state law enforcement agencies in August 2020, it said. The statement also said one of the victims of Stanisław P. had notified the District Prosecutor’s Office in Opole, southwestern Poland, about the alleged crimes in 2010. In the second case, the Curia said Bishop Jeż was only notified that Fr. Tomasz K. had allegedly sexual abused a person under 15 towards the end of 2021, and he had notified law enforcement about it in December of that year.
